releaseNotes:
v1.0.1-preview.30
- Synchronized package version with the preview.30 release.

v1.0.1-preview.29
- BREAKING: the OAuth redirect URI is now `{applicationId}:oauth2redirect` — the application id verbatim as the URI scheme (previously the reverse-DNS of the package name, e.g. `app.example.com:oauth2redirect`). Migration: update OAuth provider allowlists (e.g. the provider console's authorized redirect URLs) to the new URI, and remove any manual `Import` of `build/FireForNet.Firebase.Auth.Android.targets` from ProjectReference-based apps — that file is gone and nothing replaces it.
- BREAKING (behavior): `EnableWebAuthProvider` now defaults to `true` (web sign-in on by default, matching the official SDKs where the capability is always available). Set it to `false` to opt out.
- Zero-setup OAuth redirect: the package manifest-merges the `FireForNetOAuthRedirectActivity` trampoline and its intent-filter scheme resolves from the built-in `${applicationId}` manifest placeholder. No manifest edits and no `OnNewIntent` forwarding code are required; manual forwarding to `HandleCallbackAsync` remains supported.
- The activity context now self-attaches via `Application.RegisterActivityLifecycleCallbacks` on first use; an explicit `Attach` call remains supported and takes precedence.
- Unsolicited redirect intents (no pending sign-in, or wrong scheme) complete nothing, leave no state, and cannot burn a pending sign-in flow. Known limitation: a well-formed spoof using the matching scheme can still consume a pending flow; a per-flow `state` nonce is planned.
- Fixes a cancellation-registration lifetime bug in `CustomTabsWebAuthProvider.SignInAsync` where the cancellation callback's registration was disposed before the flow completed.

v1.0.1-preview.28
- Synchronized package version with the preview.28 release.

v1.0.1-preview.27
- Fixes token persistence on Android. EncryptedFile.openFileOutput() refuses to overwrite an existing file ("output file already exists, please use a new file"), so every token refresh after the first sign-in threw IOException. StoreAsync now replaces the file (delete-then-write), the only overwrite path the Jetpack Security API offers.
- Storage failures now surface as AndroidFirebaseAuthException instead of raw IOException or GeneralSecurityException, matching the one-exception-per-package rule.
- The loopback emulator defaults (localhost and 127.0.0.1) now resolve to 10.0.2.2 automatically on Android at service registration (FirebaseEmulatorHosts.Resolve in Core), so the default configuration works inside an AVD with no Android-specific code. Mirrors the official Flutter SDK's automaticHostMapping. Every other host is respected verbatim; set AutomaticHostMapping = false on the builder to keep loopback addresses verbatim, e.g. for adb reverse setups. The per-package FirebaseEmulatorHosts constant introduced earlier in this release is superseded by the Core resolver.
- Fixes session restore on Android, which preview.26 did not. KeystoreTokenStorage.RetrieveAsync no longer throws when reading persisted tokens. EncryptedFile.OpenFileInput() is bound to System.IO.Stream, whose InputStreamInvoker calls FileInputStream.getChannel() on the peer; EncryptedFileInputStream extends FileInputStream, so the binding threw Java.Lang.UnsupportedOperationException ("For encrypted files, please open the relevant FileInput/FileOutputStream.") before a single byte was read (dotnet/android-libraries#405). Reads now go through EncryptedFileStreamHelper, which calls the Java openFileInput method directly and keeps the peer typed as InputStream, so getChannel() is never reached. Writes were never affected, which is why the failure only surfaced on the second launch.

v1.0.1-preview.26
- Introduced EncryptedFileStreamHelper so KeystoreTokenStorage.RetrieveAsync reads persisted tokens without going through EncryptedFile.OpenFileInput(), the binding that triggers the FileInputStream.getChannel() defect (dotnet/android-libraries#405). Note: this release did NOT fix session restore. The helper hardcoded the JNI descriptor as "()Ljava/io/InputStream;" while openFileInput() is declared to return java.io.FileInputStream, so the lookup failed with Java.Lang.NoSuchMethodError instead. Fixed in preview.27.
